cells.tense: You are here, at the end of something, with the pen still in your hand.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Leave an hour unclaimed today — no plan in it — and greet whatever turns up the way you'd greet a guest already at the door.
cells.core:
Something has finished, and you're living in the part that's done rather than waiting on a verdict. The road ahead is lit by what you genuinely want, not by what you're supposed to want, and that light is enough to walk by. One stretch ending didn't dim the next. It's what made the next visible.

What comes next is arriving already. Meet it as it arrives, not as you rehearsed it. Leave an hour unclaimed. Don't fill it with a plan. What turns up in that hour is new, and it can be received the way this ending was received: whole, and on time. The cycle closes and stays open. That isn't a contradiction here. It's how you keep moving.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is real, and it opened the road.
cells.verb: closing a thing fully and turning toward what comes next
cells.place: on a road lit ahead of you by something you actually want

cells.tense: You will have arrived at a place you haven't reached yet.
cells.act: receive the thing that is coming instead of bracing for it
cells.ask: Go back once to an unfinished piece of something you've already declared done — no verdict on it, just receive what's actually there.
cells.core:
You're calling it done before the last part has landed. The road is lit by something you want, and you're already standing at its end in your head, announcing an arrival that hasn't happened. What's still moving gets declared complete so the waiting can stop. That's not finishing. That's skipping the part where it finishes.

Underneath the hurry is a future you're bracing against, one you can't write from here no matter how far ahead you lean. Some part of this got closed too early. Go back to an open piece of it — not the whole thing — and receive what's actually there instead of what you've already decided is there. The road doesn't need you at its end. It needs you where it is. What arrives on time arrives; what you drag forward arrives hollow.
cells.sheetLine: You called it finished before it was, so the finish is hollow.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Choose a stretch you keep describing as still ahead, and let one line settle what already ended inside it — then stop there.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you're still at its door. The road ahead is lit — there's a direction you actually want — but your feet haven't moved toward it in a while. Cycles get held open past their close, so nothing ends and nothing starts, and the seeking has become the thing you do. The wanted thing stays wanted, unreached.

A turning is what changes that, and a turning can be small. Take one you keep saying is still ahead of you — still coming, still pending — and let one line settle what already finished inside it. No plan after it. Let that end be an end. When one door is allowed closed, the road shows itself again, and the light you were steering by comes back into view. It was there the whole while. Both hands were on the old handle.
cells.sheetLine: You're at a door that already closed.

cells.place: on a road lit ahead of you by something you actually want

cells.tense: You are writing in a room you don't remember entering, pen already down.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Set down what you're still holding past its finish, tonight, and notice where the empty hands want to go.
cells.core:
You've been steering by a light you've not stopped to name. Some things in your life ended and you didn't mark them; some didn't end and you've been treating them as done. Either way you're moving without knowing which road you're on or why it's lit. The light is still there. You haven't looked up at it in a while.

There's something you're still gripping — whose time has passed, or whose ending you didn't quite agree to. Set it down. Not by losing it, not by declaring it over with a speech. Stop holding it, for tonight. Leave your hands empty and see where they want to go, because the want that's been steering you sits underneath the grip, and it can't be felt through it. Letting go here isn't a loss. It's what makes the next arrival visible.

attempts.check: The draft leans on the idea that the person can name what has finished in their life; the record supports only that completion-integration is the capacity at issue, not that they will recognize it on request. A reader could say the ending is obvious and ordinary, or that nothing in their life looks finished at all. The ask survives being wrong either way: meeting the next arriving thing, or naming what's done, is usable even if my read of their situation is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that would rather be beautiful about thresholds than plain about the next hour.
